Egypt: Gateway to Africa.q: According to the article, Egypt serves as a bridge among Africa, the Middle East and ______.
Egypt: Gateway to Africa.e: The article says Egypt is a bridge among the African continent, the Middle East, and Europe.

Egypt: Gateway to Africa.q: Which of these is NOT mentioned as an infrastructure project connecting Egypt with its southern neighbors?
Egypt: Gateway to Africa.e: The projects listed are road networks, telecommunications systems and energy partnerships.

Egypt: Gateway to Africa.q: Egypt offers scholarships to African students who want to ______.
Egypt: Gateway to Africa.e: The article says Egypt offers scholarships to African students who want to study at Egyptian universities.

Egypt: Gateway to Africa.q: What does Egypt import from countries like the Sudan, Uganda and Kenya?
Egypt: Gateway to Africa.e: In return for its exports, Egypt imports raw materials and natural resources from these countries.

Egypt: Gateway to Africa.q: Egypt combines medical aid with capacity building in order to ______.
Egypt: Gateway to Africa.e: Egypt aims not only to treat patients but also to empower local health systems.

o: goods made on a large scale using machinery
the basic structures and facilities like roads and power supplies
a point of entry to something larger
Egypt: Gateway to Africa.e: Infrastructure is the basic physical structures and facilities, such as buildings, roads and power supplies.

Egypt: Gateway to Africa.q: This mutual exchange is creating jobs. The word "mutual" means ______.
o: done by each party toward the other
Egypt: Gateway to Africa.e: Mutual means experienced or done by each of two or more parties toward the other.

Voices from the Partnership.q: Places in the countryside, away from big cities, are called ______ areas.
Voices from the Partnership.e: Rural means places in the countryside, away from big cities.

Voices from the Partnership.q: Money that is given to support a project, business or activity is ______.
Voices from the Partnership.e: Funding is money given to support a project, business or activity.

Voices from the Partnership.q: A mix of two different things, especially to make something better, is a ______.
Voices from the Partnership.e: Hybrid means a mix of two different things, especially to make something better.

Voices from the Partnership.q: Egypt is ______ its trade with African countries by spreading it to more places.
Voices from the Partnership.e: Expanding means making something bigger or spreading it to more places.

Voices from the Partnership.q: The process of bringing different groups or systems together to work as one is ______.
Voices from the Partnership.e: Integration is the process of bringing different groups or systems together to work as one.

Voices from the Partnership.q: The economy stayed ______ for years, not changing too much.
Voices from the Partnership.e: Stable means not changing too much; strong and steady.

Voices from the Partnership.q: Which useful phrase from the role-play means "we agree"?
o: We see eye to eye on...
Our countries have been cooperating since...
Voices from the Partnership.e: To see eye to eye means to agree with someone.

Listening & Grammar: Present Continuous.q: Look! The children ______ in the garden now.
Listening & Grammar: Present Continuous.e: We use the present continuous (am/is/are + verb-ing) for situations going on now.

Listening & Grammar: Present Continuous.q: A new hospital ______ in our town at the moment.
Listening & Grammar: Present Continuous.e: The present continuous passive is am/is/are + being + past participle; 'hospital' is singular.

Listening & Grammar: Present Continuous.q: The present continuous passive is formed with ______.
Listening & Grammar: Present Continuous.e: The book gives the form am / is / are + being + past participle.

Listening & Grammar: Present Continuous.q: We ______ a party at eight o'clock tomorrow. (a future arrangement)
Listening & Grammar: Present Continuous.e: The present continuous is used for actions arranged for a specific time in the future.

Listening & Grammar: Present Continuous.q: Choose the passive of: "They are building a bridge."
Listening & Grammar: Present Continuous.e: Active present continuous becomes is/are + being + past participle in the passive.

Listening & Grammar: Present Continuous.q: "Rodayna is always doing the dishes." Here the present continuous shows ______.
o: an action done to the subject
an action people do again and again
Listening & Grammar: Present Continuous.e: With 'always', the present continuous describes an action that people do again and again.

Listening & Grammar: Present Continuous.q: Many new roads ______ across Africa these days.
Listening & Grammar: Present Continuous.e: 'Roads' is plural and receives the action, so we use are + being + past participle.

Success Stories in African Partnership.q: Since when has the Egypt-Sudan Agricultural Project been transforming farming communities?
Success Stories in African Partnership.e: The passage says the project has been transforming farming communities since 2019.

Success Stories in African Partnership.q: What was the result of the Egypt-Sudan Agricultural Project in targeted areas?
Success Stories in African Partnership.e: Modern irrigation and better yields resulted in a 35% increase in food production.

Success Stories in African Partnership.q: Which project was cited as a milestone showing Egypt's expanding expertise?
Success Stories in African Partnership.e: A major dam project in Tanzania built by Egyptian companies was cited as a milestone.

Success Stories in African Partnership.q: How many jobs have the Egyptian-Kenyan solar projects created?
Success Stories in African Partnership.e: The solar panel projects have created over 5,000 jobs.

Success Stories in African Partnership.q: The African film festival in Cairo features films from ______ African nations.
Success Stories in African Partnership.e: The annual festival, launched in 2018, features films from 25 African nations.

Success Stories in African Partnership.q: Egyptian medical teams build sustainable capacity by ______.
Success Stories in African Partnership.e: Medical teams deliver healthcare and train local staff, building sustainable capacity.

Success Stories in African Partnership.q: The solar projects help to reduce reliance on ______.
Success Stories in African Partnership.e: The passage says the solar projects are helping reduce reliance on fossil fuels.

Writing: An Essay.q: An essay has three main parts: introduction, body paragraphs and ______.
Writing: An Essay.e: The tip box lists introduction, body paragraphs and conclusion.

Writing: An Essay.q: The sentence in the introduction that tells the reader exactly what the essay is about is the ______.
Writing: An Essay.e: The thesis statement is the most important sentence in the introduction and gives the main point.

Writing: An Essay.q: Each body paragraph should start with a ______.
Writing: An Essay.e: Start each body paragraph with a topic sentence that introduces its idea.

Writing: An Essay.q: How many body paragraphs should an essay have at least?
Writing: An Essay.e: You should write at least two or three body paragraphs.

Writing: An Essay.q: What is the job of the "hook" in an introduction?
Writing: An Essay.e: The hook grabs the reader's attention with an interesting sentence.

Writing: An Essay.q: Which sentence would best begin a conclusion?
o: In conclusion, dogs make wonderful pets.
Dogs are great pets for many reasons.
Another reason is that dogs protect your home.
Writing: An Essay.e: A conclusion restates the thesis in a new way, often starting with 'In conclusion'.

Writing: An Essay.q: Each body paragraph should focus on ______.
o: all the ideas of the essay
one single idea supporting the main point
Writing: An Essay.e: Each body paragraph should focus on one single idea that supports the main point.

Inspiring Entrepreneurs.q: What was special about Bank Misr?
o: It was created with completely Egyptian capital.
It was run by foreign experts.
It was the first bank in Africa.
Inspiring Entrepreneurs.e: Bank Misr was a bank created with completely Egyptian capital.

Inspiring Entrepreneurs.q: How many Egyptians did Talaat Harb convince to invest in the project?
Inspiring Entrepreneurs.e: He convinced more than 120 Egyptians to invest and secure the necessary capital.

Inspiring Entrepreneurs.q: Which industries did Talaat Harb's team support with Egyptian capital?
Inspiring Entrepreneurs.e: Egyptian capital was used to support shipping, aviation and filmmaking.

Inspiring Entrepreneurs.q: According to the article, the key to success lies in ______.
o: investing a lot of money quickly
Inspiring Entrepreneurs.e: Successful founders identify real social needs and address them; the key lies in solving real problems.

o: starts or creates a business or organization
Inspiring Entrepreneurs.e: A founder is a person who starts or creates a business, organization or company.

Inspiring Entrepreneurs.q: Choose the correct collocation from the passage.
Inspiring Entrepreneurs.e: The correct pairs are take risks, solve problems, face challenges and achieve success.

Startup Pitch Competition.q: Giving a short, persuasive talk for investors, partners or customers is called ______.
Startup Pitch Competition.e: Pitching means giving a short, persuasive talk for investors, partners or customers.

Startup Pitch Competition.q: A list or count of all the goods a business has for sale is its ______.
Startup Pitch Competition.e: Inventory is a list or count of all the goods, items or products a business has for sale.

Startup Pitch Competition.q: Paying to use something for a short time is called ______.
Startup Pitch Competition.e: Rental means paying to use something for a short time.
Tutoring is helping someone learn one-on-one.

Startup Pitch Competition.q: The traditional approach wasn't working, so we had to "think outside the box". This means ______.
o: think in a new, creative way
Startup Pitch Competition.e: To think outside the box means to think creatively and in new ways.

Startup Pitch Competition.q: According to the listening task, what problem did Pitch 1 try to solve?
Startup Pitch Competition.e: The listening task states Pitch 1's problem: food waste in restaurants.

Startup Pitch Competition.q: Pitch 3 offered a clothing rental service to solve ______.
Startup Pitch Competition.e: The listening task states Pitch 3's problem: fast fashion's environmental impact.

Listening & Grammar: Past Perfect (Activ.q: The past perfect active is formed with ______.
Listening & Grammar: Past Perfect (Activ.e: Use the past perfect (had + past participle) for an action before another past action.

Listening & Grammar: Past Perfect (Activ.q: I ______ the shopping before I returned home.
Listening & Grammar: Past Perfect (Activ.e: The shopping happened before returning home, so we use the past perfect.

Listening & Grammar: Past Perfect (Activ.q: The reports ______ well before they were sent to the manager.
Listening & Grammar: Past Perfect (Activ.e: The past perfect passive (had been + p.p.) is used when the agent is unimportant or unknown.

Listening & Grammar: Past Perfect (Activ.q: Sama thought she ______ the housework, but she had forgotten the washing up.
Listening & Grammar: Past Perfect (Activ.e: The past perfect is often used after verbs like thought and realized for earlier actions.

Listening & Grammar: Past Perfect (Activ.q: Before launching his business, Omar ______ environmental engineering at Alexandria University.
Listening & Grammar: Past Perfect (Activ.e: Studying happened before launching the business, so the past perfect active is used.

Listening & Grammar: Past Perfect (Activ.q: Within a year, his products ______ in more than fifty cafés.
Listening & Grammar: Past Perfect (Activ.e: Products do not use; they are used, so we need the past perfect passive had been + p.p.

Listening & Grammar: Past Perfect (Activ.q: Many single-use plastics ______ in some cities before his products reached the market.
Listening & Grammar: Past Perfect (Activ.e: The banning happened earlier and the agent is not important, so had been banned is correct.

Small Places, Big Impact!.q: About what percentage of Egypt's population lives in villages?
Small Places, Big Impact!.e: The passage says Egypt's 4,740 villages house about 57% of the population.

Small Places, Big Impact!.q: How many villages are there in Egypt, according to the passage?
Small Places, Big Impact!.e: The passage states there are 4,740 villages in Egypt.

Small Places, Big Impact!.q: Which village is notable for producing a large portion of the world's jasmine?
Small Places, Big Impact!.e: Shubra Beloula produces a large portion of the world's jasmine for perfumes.

Small Places, Big Impact!.q: Sidi Heneish figs are described as organic because they are grown ______.
Small Places, Big Impact!.e: Sidi Heneish's organic figs are grown without pesticides and with rainwater.

Small Places, Big Impact!.q: Baharif in Aswan is recognized for its ______.
Small Places, Big Impact!.e: Baharif is recognized for its date palms, around 300,000 trees.

Small Places, Big Impact!.q: Shubra Mellas in Gharbia exports flax to countries like ______.
Small Places, Big Impact!.e: Shubra Mellas is Egypt's largest flax-producing village, exporting to China and Belgium.

Small Places, Big Impact!.q: How do village industries help young people?
o: by providing jobs and increasing income
Small Places, Big Impact!.e: Village industries and crafts increase family incomes and provide jobs for young people.

Writing: A Business Email.q: A business email is different from a personal email because it ______.
Writing: A Business Email.e: Business emails follow a more formal and polite format to keep professionalism and clarity.

Writing: A Business Email.q: Which greeting should you use if you don't know the person's name?
Writing: A Business Email.e: The tip box gives 'Dear Sir/Madam,' when the name is unknown.

Writing: A Business Email.q: Which sign-off is correct if you used the person's name in the greeting?
Writing: A Business Email.e: Use 'Yours sincerely' if you used their name and 'Yours faithfully' if you didn't.

Writing: A Business Email.q: Which of these is a polite request?
o: I would appreciate it if you could send the report.
I hope this email finds you well.
Writing: A Business Email.e: 'I would appreciate it if you could...' is listed among polite requests.

Writing: A Business Email.q: In Sarah Lee's email, what is the purpose of writing?
o: to thank Mr. Thompson for a gift
to request a meeting about the City Park project
Writing: A Business Email.e: She writes to request a meeting to discuss the progress of the City Park project.

Writing: A Business Email.q: A good subject line in a business email should be ______.
Writing: A Business Email.e: The tip box says to keep the subject line short and clear.

Writing: A Business Email.q: Complete the closing phrase: "I look forward to ______."
Writing: A Business Email.e: 'I look forward to your reply' is a standard closing phrase.

Egypt Vision 2030.q: According to the article, the Sustainable Development Strategy (SDS) is ______.
o: a plan to build new cities only
a long-term plan to improve people's lives fairly
Egypt Vision 2030.e: SDS means a long-term plan that focuses on improving people's lives in a fair and balanced way.

Egypt Vision 2030.q: What are the three main pillars of the SDS?
o: the economy, society and the environment
Egypt Vision 2030.e: The SDS focuses on three main pillars: the economy, society and the environment.

Egypt Vision 2030.q: Who worked together to design the SDS plan?
o: civil society, government agencies and local and international partners
Egypt Vision 2030.e: Civil society, government agencies and local and international partners all worked together to design the plan.

Egypt Vision 2030.q: Why does the SDS give Egypt an advantage in addressing global changes?
o: because Egypt has the most oil
because of Egypt's unique position in the region and the world
Egypt Vision 2030.e: Because of Egypt's unique position in the region and the world, the SDS gives it an advantage.

o: important parts or strong supports of a system
Egypt Vision 2030.e: Pillars are important parts or strong supports of a system, idea or structure.

Egypt Vision 2030.q: "Comprehensive" national development means development that is ______.
o: covering all or nearly all aspects
Egypt Vision 2030.e: Comprehensive means complete and covering all or nearly all aspects of something.

Egypt Vision 2030.q: Inclusive and balanced development means that every person should ______.
o: take part in development and benefit from it equally
Egypt Vision 2030.e: Every person should take part in development, benefit from it equally and have fair opportunities.

Egypt's Path to Better Healthcare.q: A long-term disease, like diabetes or asthma, is called a ______ disease.
Egypt's Path to Better Healthcare.e: A chronic disease is a long-term disease like diabetes or asthma.

Egypt's Path to Better Healthcare.q: Checking people for diseases before they show symptoms is called ______.
Egypt's Path to Better Healthcare.e: Screening means checking people for diseases before they show symptoms.

Egypt's Path to Better Healthcare.q: A new plan or program started to solve a problem is an ______.
Egypt's Path to Better Healthcare.e: An initiative is a new plan or program started to solve a problem.

o: fair and equal opportunities for all to get the same services
Egypt's Path to Better Healthcare.e: Equitable access means fair and equal opportunities for all to get the same services.

Egypt's Path to Better Healthcare.q: The percentage of people who have received vaccines is called ______.
Egypt's Path to Better Healthcare.e: Vaccination coverage is the percentage of people who have received vaccines.

o: relating to or done by all people
Egypt's Path to Better Healthcare.e: Universal means relating to or done by all people or things in the world.

Listening & Grammar: Adjectives and Adve.e: An adverb describes the verb 'speaks' and answers the question 'how?'.
After 'taste' (a sense verb) we describe the noun 'soup', so we use the adjective.

Listening & Grammar: Adjectives and Adve.q: Find the mistake: "He is a carefully driver."
Listening & Grammar: Adjectives and Adve.e: 'Driver' is a noun, so it needs the adjective 'careful', not the adverb.

o: What kind? Which one? How many?
Listening & Grammar: Adjectives and Adve.e: Adjectives describe nouns and answer What kind?, Which one? and How many?

Listening & Grammar: Adjectives and Adve.q: In "It was very cold", the word "very" is an adverb that shows ______.
Listening & Grammar: Adjectives and Adve.e: The book's example 'It was very cold' shows an adverb of extent modifying an adjective.

Listening & Grammar: Adjectives and Adve.q: The cat moved ______ through the room.
Listening & Grammar: Adjectives and Adve.e: The adverb 'silently' describes how the cat moved (the verb).

Listening & Grammar: Adjectives and Adve.q: It was a ______ day, so we stayed inside.

Education in Egypt Vision 2030.q: Education is described as a "cornerstone" of Egypt Vision 2030. "Cornerstone" means ______.
Education in Egypt Vision 2030.e: A cornerstone is the foundation, the most basic and important part of something.

Education in Egypt Vision 2030.q: Curricula are being redesigned to focus on creativity and critical thinking rather than ______.
Education in Egypt Vision 2030.e: The passage says curricula focus on creativity, critical thinking and problem-solving rather than rote memorization.

Education in Egypt Vision 2030.q: New technologies have been introduced in classrooms to ______ the learning experience.
Education in Egypt Vision 2030.e: Technologies were introduced to enhance, or improve, the learning experience.

Education in Egypt Vision 2030.q: Which is one specific change in education mentioned in the passage?
Education in Egypt Vision 2030.e: Teachers are receiving continuous training to improve their teaching methods.

Education in Egypt Vision 2030.q: Which challenges to educational reform does the passage mention?
Education in Egypt Vision 2030.e: The passage says challenges such as funding and infrastructure still exist.

Education in Egypt Vision 2030.q: Egypt Vision 2030 hopes to build a generation that is capable of ______.
Education in Egypt Vision 2030.e: By 2030, the government hopes to build a generation capable of innovation and leadership.

Education in Egypt Vision 2030.q: Which is NOT one of the education goals mentioned?
Education in Egypt Vision 2030.e: The passage mentions reducing illiteracy, early childhood education and vocational training, not fewer schools.

Writing: A Blog Post.q: According to the tip box, writing a blog post is like ______.
o: telling a story to a friend
Writing: A Blog Post.e: The tip box says to think of a blog post like telling a story to a friend.

Writing: A Blog Post.q: How should you start a blog post?
o: with a hook that grabs the reader's attention
Writing: A Blog Post.e: Start with a hook that grabs the reader's attention and makes them want to read more.

Writing: A Blog Post.q: What helps break up the text of a blog post so it is easy to follow?
Writing: A Blog Post.e: The tip box advises using headings to break up your text.

Writing: A Blog Post.q: A strong blog post conclusion should ______.
o: leave the reader with something to think about or a call to action
Writing: A Blog Post.e: End with a strong conclusion that leaves the reader something to think about or a call to action.

Writing: A Blog Post.q: In the model blog post, where is the Grand Egyptian Museum located?
Writing: A Blog Post.e: The model post says the museum is located near the Pyramids of Giza.

Writing: A Blog Post.q: According to the model post, the GEM will display ______.
Writing: A Blog Post.e: The museum will display more than 100,000 artifacts, including Tutankhamun's complete collection.

Writing: A Blog Post.q: Which phrase is commonly used to express an opinion in a blog?
Writing: A Blog Post.e: 'I think' and 'I believe' express the writer's opinion.

Review 1.q: Theirs was a partnership based on mutual respect. The opposite of "mutual" is ______.
Review 1.e: Mutual means shared by both sides, so its opposite is one-sided.

Review 1.q: Farmers in dry regions benefit from ______ crops developed by scientists.
Review 1.e: Hybrid crops mix two different things to make something better.

Review 1.q: By the time we arrived at the theater, the movie ______.
Review 1.e: The movie started before we arrived, so the past perfect is used.

Review 1.q: Right now, engineers ______ a new highway to Sudan.
Review 1.e: 'Right now' shows an action going on now, so we use the present continuous.

o: The tickets had been sold out before we reached the box office.
The tickets have been sold out before we reached the box office.
The tickets was sold out before we had reached the box office.
The tickets are sold out before we had reached the box office.
Review 1.e: The earlier passive action uses had been + p.p., and the later action uses the past simple.

Review 1.q: The team worked ______ to finish the project on time.
Review 1.e: 'Hard' is the adverb meaning with great effort; 'hardly' means almost not.

Review 1.q: Organic farming avoids the use of harmful ______.
Review 1.e: Organic crops are grown without pesticides.

Review 1.q: In the review passage, entrepreneurs contribute to economic growth by ______.
o: introducing new technologies and creating jobs
Review 1.e: The passage says entrepreneurs introduce new technologies, create jobs and stimulate competition.

A Call for Adaptation.q: Which tools do meteorologists use to monitor temperature, wind, pressure and humidity?
o: satellites, radar systems and computer models
A Call for Adaptation.e: Meteorologists use satellites, radar systems and computer models to monitor the weather.

A Call for Adaptation.q: What is the result of better hurricane path forecasting?
o: Governments can organize evacuations and lives can be saved.
A Call for Adaptation.e: Better forecasting lets governments organize evacuations, hospitals prepare and lives be saved.

o: Seismic activity occurs deep beneath the Earth's surface with no clear warning signs.
A Call for Adaptation.e: Seismic activity occurs deep underground and there are usually no clear warning signs.

o: the amount of water in the air
A Call for Adaptation.e: Humidity is the amount of water in the air.

o: how strong or powerful something is
A Call for Adaptation.e: Intensity means how strong or powerful something is.

A Call for Adaptation.q: Huge pieces of Earth's surface that move and cause earthquakes are called ______.
A Call for Adaptation.e: Tectonic plates are huge pieces of Earth's surface that move and cause earthquakes.

A Call for Adaptation.q: According to the text, what remain our strongest defenses against natural disasters?
A Call for Adaptation.e: The text ends by saying readiness and planning remain our strongest defenses.

o: the state of being ready, especially for an emergency
Emergency Awareness.e: Preparedness is the state of being ready for something, especially an emergency.

Emergency Awareness.q: Food that is likely to decay or go bad quickly is called ______ food.
Emergency Awareness.e: Perishable means likely to decay or go bad quickly; it usually refers to food.

Emergency Awareness.q: Keep copies of your documents in a ______ container so water cannot pass through it.
Emergency Awareness.e: Waterproof means not allowing water to pass through it.

Emergency Awareness.q: A set of articles or equipment needed for a specific purpose is a ______.
Emergency Awareness.e: A kit is a set of articles or equipment needed for a specific purpose.

Emergency Awareness.q: "Official papers or records that provide information or proof" are ______.
Emergency Awareness.e: Documents are official papers or records that give information or proof.

Emergency Awareness.q: "We should have kept a flashlight in the kitchen." This sentence shows ______.
Emergency Awareness.e: 'Should have + past participle' talks about something that was the right thing to do but wasn't done.

o: things needed for a purpose that are provided or stored
Emergency Awareness.e: Supplies are things needed for a particular purpose that are provided or stored.

Listening & Grammar: Comparative and Sup.q: The Nile is the ______ river in the world.
Listening & Grammar: Comparative and Sup.e: Short adjectives add -est in the superlative, used with 'the' to show the highest degree.

Listening & Grammar: Comparative and Sup.q: Cairo is ______ than many other African cities.
Listening & Grammar: Comparative and Sup.e: 'Than' shows a comparison of two, so we use the comparative form busier.

Listening & Grammar: Comparative and Sup.q: Comparative adjectives are used to compare ______.
Listening & Grammar: Comparative and Sup.e: Comparative adjectives compare two things or people.

Listening & Grammar: Comparative and Sup.q: This is ______ phone I've ever had.
Listening & Grammar: Comparative and Sup.e: 'Good' is irregular: good, better, the best.
Long adjectives use 'more' in the comparative form.
'Bad' is irregular: bad, worse, the worst.
Superlatives show the highest degree among three or more; short adjectives add -est.

Preparing for Natural Disasters.q: What is the main idea of the passage "Learning from the Past"?
o: what to do during an earthquake
Preparing for Natural Disasters.e: The passage teaches that being prepared saves lives.

Preparing for Natural Disasters.q: In what year did the powerful storm hit the small coastal town?
Preparing for Natural Disasters.e: The passage says that in 2023 a powerful storm hit a small coastal town.

Preparing for Natural Disasters.q: "People realized that they should have listened to the early warnings." This shows that people ______.
o: made a mistake in the past
Preparing for Natural Disasters.e: 'Should have listened' shows they did not listen, which was a mistake.

Preparing for Natural Disasters.q: What could schools and hospitals have done before the storm season?
Preparing for Natural Disasters.e: The passage says schools and hospitals could have practiced evacuation drills.

Preparing for Natural Disasters.q: Disaster preparedness includes all of the following EXCEPT ______.
Preparing for Natural Disasters.e: Preparedness includes making a plan, staying informed and taking action before it's too late.
The storm blocked roads, meaning they were closed and people could not pass.
The passage ends with the saying 'Better safe than sorry.'

Writing: A Formal Report.q: Which part of a formal report presents facts or problems discovered during research?
Writing: A Formal Report.e: Findings present the facts or problems discovered during research or observation.

Writing: A Formal Report.q: The part of a report that offers clear advice based on the findings is the ______.
Writing: A Formal Report.e: Recommendations offer clear advice or suggestions based on the findings.

Writing: A Formal Report.q: Which form is correct in a formal report?
Writing: A Formal Report.e: Formal reports use no contractions, e.g. 'do not' instead of 'don't'.

Writing: A Formal Report.q: Which phrase is suitable for the introduction of a report?
o: The purpose of this report is to...
Writing: A Formal Report.e: 'This report examines...' and 'The purpose of this report is to...' are introduction phrases.

Writing: A Formal Report.q: Which phrase is used in the conclusion of a report?
Writing: A Formal Report.e: Conclusion phrases include 'In conclusion', 'To summarize' and 'It is recommended that...'.

Writing: A Formal Report.q: Reports use headings and bullet points in order to ______.
Writing: A Formal Report.e: An organized structure with headings and bullet points makes information easy to read.

Writing: A Formal Report.q: What does the "Introduction" of a formal report do?
o: briefly explains the purpose of the report
Writing: A Formal Report.e: The introduction briefly explains the purpose of the report.

The Anatomy of Fake News.q: According to a recent study in the text, false news stories spread ______ than true stories on social media.
The Anatomy of Fake News.e: The study found false news spreads six times faster on social media than true stories.

The Anatomy of Fake News.q: According to the expert, the first red flag of fake news is ______.
o: sensational headlines designed to trigger strong emotions
The Anatomy of Fake News.e: The expert says the first red flag is sensational headlines designed to trigger strong emotions.

The Anatomy of Fake News.q: Which is a characteristic of reliable journalism?
o: citing information and giving publication dates
The Anatomy of Fake News.e: Reliable sources cite their information, quote multiple views and provide publication dates.

The Anatomy of Fake News.q: What are "echo chambers" created by social media algorithms?
o: places where you mostly see things that agree with what you think
The Anatomy of Fake News.e: Echo chambers mean you mostly see stuff that already agrees with what you think.
Misleading means giving the wrong idea or impression; deceptive.

The Anatomy of Fake News.q: A set of rules a computer follows to solve a problem is called ______.
The Anatomy of Fake News.e: Algorithms are a set of rules or instructions that a computer follows.

The Anatomy of Fake News.q: Which piece of advice does the expert give to news consumers?
o: Check more than one source before you trust it.
Trust the first source you see.
Believe stories that sound too good to be true.
The Anatomy of Fake News.e: He advises checking more than one source before you trust it.

Social Media Regulation.q: A rule or law made by a government to control how something is done is a ______.
Social Media Regulation.e: Regulation is a rule or law made by a government or authority to control how something is done.

o: to make sure something is true or correct
Social Media Regulation.e: To verify is to make sure something is true, accurate or correct.

Social Media Regulation.q: The act of tricking someone or making them believe something untrue is ______.
Social Media Regulation.e: Deception is the act of tricking someone into believing something that is not true.

Social Media Regulation.q: The quality of being open, honest and easy to understand, with no secrets, is ______.
Social Media Regulation.e: Transparency is the quality of being open, honest and easy to understand.

Social Media Regulation.q: A limit or control on something is a ______.
Social Media Regulation.e: A restriction is a limit or control on something.

o: the act of taking something away
Social Media Regulation.e: Removal is the act of taking something away.

Social Media Regulation.q: Which useful phrase shows that you partly doubt an idea?
o: Professor Chen makes a persuasive point about...
I tend to agree with Dr. Park because...
Social Media Regulation.e: 'I'm not entirely convinced that...' expresses doubt about an argument.

Listening & Grammar: Tag Questions.e: A positive statement takes a negative tag with the same auxiliary (does).
A negative statement takes a positive tag; the auxiliary is 'has'.

Listening & Grammar: Tag Questions.q: Babies can hardly depend on themselves, ______?
Listening & Grammar: Tag Questions.e: Tags are affirmative after words like hardly, nobody and nothing.

Listening & Grammar: Tag Questions.q: Not all media is trying to trick us, ______?
Listening & Grammar: Tag Questions.e: The statement is negative, so the tag is positive: is it?

Listening & Grammar: Tag Questions.q: When the speaker is sure the statement is true, the intonation of the tag ______.
Listening & Grammar: Tag Questions.e: When the speaker is sure the statement is true, the intonation falls.

Listening & Grammar: Tag Questions.q: Find the mistake: "She's your sister, doesn't she?"
Listening & Grammar: Tag Questions.e: 'She's' means 'she is', so the correct tag is 'isn't she?'.
With a modal, we repeat the modal in the tag: shouldn't they?

How Media Shapes Our Choices.q: What is the main idea of "The Puppet Masters"?
o: Social media is the best way to stay informed.
People should stop using the internet.
Media subtly shapes thoughts and behaviors using psychological techniques.
How Media Shapes Our Choices.e: The text explains that modern media uses subtle psychological techniques to influence behavior.

How Media Shapes Our Choices.q: Words like "shocking" or "unbelievable" are chosen to ______.
How Media Shapes Our Choices.e: These words are carefully chosen to spark strong feelings.

How Media Shapes Our Choices.q: What is the effect of "either-or" framing?
o: It shows all the details of a topic.
It reduces curiosity by simplifying topics into two extreme options.
How Media Shapes Our Choices.e: Either-or framing simplifies complex topics into two extremes, reducing curiosity.

How Media Shapes Our Choices.q: Phrases like "going viral" or "everyone is trying this" are examples of ______.
How Media Shapes Our Choices.e: Social proof uses such phrases to create a sense of urgency and belonging.

How Media Shapes Our Choices.q: How do algorithms create a feedback loop?
o: by showing content similar to what users engaged with before
How Media Shapes Our Choices.e: Algorithms show content similar to past engagement, reinforcing existing preferences.

How Media Shapes Our Choices.q: Why is attention described as the most valuable resource in the digital age?
o: Companies profit when users click, watch or share content.
How Media Shapes Our Choices.e: The text says attention is the most valuable resource; companies profit when users click, watch or share content.

How Media Shapes Our Choices.q: Liking or sharing content "without reflection" means doing it ______.
How Media Shapes Our Choices.e: Reflection means careful thought; emotional responses can override critical thinking.

Writing: An Opinion Essay.q: What is the aim of an opinion essay?
o: to persuade the reader to understand and agree with an opinion
Writing: An Opinion Essay.e: An opinion essay aims to persuade the reader to understand and potentially agree with the opinion.

Writing: An Opinion Essay.q: The introduction of an opinion essay includes a hook, background and ______.
Writing: An Opinion Essay.e: The introduction contains a hook, background and thesis statement.

Writing: An Opinion Essay.q: Which part of an opinion essay presents the opposing view?
Writing: An Opinion Essay.e: The counter-argument paragraph presents the opposing view.

Writing: An Opinion Essay.q: Which phrase is used for giving examples?
Writing: An Opinion Essay.e: 'For example' is listed among the phrases for giving examples.

Writing: An Opinion Essay.q: "Secondly, phones can cause health problems." This sentence belongs to ______.
Writing: An Opinion Essay.e: 'Secondly' introduces the second reason in the body.

Writing: An Opinion Essay.q: The conclusion of an opinion essay includes a summary, a final opinion and ______.
Writing: An Opinion Essay.e: The conclusion contains a summary, final opinion and future prediction.

Writing: An Opinion Essay.q: Which phrase is suitable for giving a final opinion?
Writing: An Opinion Essay.e: 'That's why I strongly believe...' is listed for stating a final opinion.

Soft Skills vs. Hard Skills.q: According to the article, hard skills are ______.
o: technical abilities or knowledge learned through education or training
Soft Skills vs. Hard Skills.e: Hard skills are the technical abilities or knowledge you learn through education or training.

Soft Skills vs. Hard Skills.q: Which of these is a soft skill?
Soft Skills vs. Hard Skills.e: Soft skills include communication, teamwork, time management, problem-solving and leadership.

Soft Skills vs. Hard Skills.q: Hard skills can often be proved with ______.
o: certificates, tests or examples of work
Soft Skills vs. Hard Skills.e: Hard skills are often measurable and proved with certificates, tests or examples of work.

Soft Skills vs. Hard Skills.q: Why do employers say soft skills are harder to develop?
o: They involve personality, attitude and emotional intelligence.
Soft Skills vs. Hard Skills.e: Soft skills are harder to develop because they involve personality, attitude and emotional intelligence.

Soft Skills vs. Hard Skills.q: According to the article, hard skills help you get hired, but soft skills help you ______.
Soft Skills vs. Hard Skills.e: In short, hard skills help you get hired, but soft skills help you grow in your career.
Reliable means trustworthy and consistently good in quality or performance.

Soft Skills vs. Hard Skills.q: A "brilliant" programmer is one who is ______.
Soft Skills vs. Hard Skills.e: Brilliant means exceptionally intelligent, skilled or impressive.

Radio Debate.q: A person who can recover quickly from difficulties is ______.
Radio Debate.e: Resilient means able to recover quickly from difficulties or challenges.

Radio Debate.q: Someone with a strong desire to succeed or achieve something important is ______.
Radio Debate.e: Ambitious means having a strong desire to succeed or achieve something important.

Radio Debate.q: A person who is willing to work with others and help as part of a team is ______.
Radio Debate.e: Cooperative means willing to work with others and help as part of a team.

o: be trusted to do things on time
use imagination and original ideas to make something new
Radio Debate.e: Creative means able to use imagination and original ideas to make or do something new.

Radio Debate.q: Which word is closest in meaning to "vital"?
Radio Debate.e: Vital means extremely important or absolutely needed, like essential.

Radio Debate.q: A person who can be trusted to do something well or on time is ______.
Radio Debate.e: Reliable means can be trusted to do something well or on time.

Listening & Grammar: Defining and Non-de.q: Ahmed is the student ______ got full marks.
Listening & Grammar: Defining and Non-de.e: We use 'who' (or 'that') for people in defining relative clauses.

Listening & Grammar: Defining and Non-de.q: The new building, ______ is solar-powered, opened last October.
Listening & Grammar: Defining and Non-de.e: In non-defining clauses we cannot use 'that'; 'which' is used for things.

Listening & Grammar: Defining and Non-de.q: Yara, ______ father was a teacher, is a clever doctor.
In which type of relative clause can we omit the relative pronoun?
o: a defining clause when the pronoun defines the object
a defining clause when the pronoun defines the subject
Listening & Grammar: Defining and Non-de.e: We can omit the relative pronoun if it defines the object, e.g. the glory (that) we inherited.

o: give necessary information and use no commas
give extra information and use commas
Listening & Grammar: Defining and Non-de.e: Non-defining clauses give extra, not important information and use commas.

Listening & Grammar: Defining and Non-de.q: Find the mistake: "The teacher which explained the lesson is from Alexandria."
Listening & Grammar: Defining and Non-de.e: 'Teacher' is a person, so we use 'who' or 'that', not 'which'.

Listening & Grammar: Defining and Non-de.q: That is the school ______ we studied last year.
Listening & Grammar: Defining and Non-de.e: 'Where' is used for places: we studied in that school.

Why Soft Skills Matter.q: According to the passage, how do soft skills grow?
Why Soft Skills Matter.e: Soft skills are not learned from books; they grow through practice and real-life experience.

Why Soft Skills Matter.q: To improve your communication, the passage suggests you could ______.
Why Soft Skills Matter.e: You could join a school debate or practice speaking in front of others.

Why Soft Skills Matter.q: To "step out of your comfort zone" means to ______.
o: leave your safe habits and try something new
Why Soft Skills Matter.e: A comfort zone is where you feel safe; stepping out means trying something new.

Why Soft Skills Matter.q: Which helps you "stay on top of things"?
o: a planner or a to-do list
Why Soft Skills Matter.e: You can use a planner or make a to-do list to stay on top of things.
To think on your feet is to make good decisions quickly when something unexpected happens.

o: your own feelings and the feelings of others
Why Soft Skills Matter.e: Emotional intelligence means understanding your own feelings and the feelings of others.

Why Soft Skills Matter.q: In a group project, you "meet others halfway". This means you ______.
Why Soft Skills Matter.e: To meet others halfway is to compromise or make concessions to reach an agreement.

o: describing a person, place, event or experience in vivid detail
Writing: A Descriptive Essay.e: A descriptive essay describes a person, place, object, event or experience in vivid detail.

Writing: A Descriptive Essay.q: Words that make you see, hear, smell, taste or feel something are called ______.
Writing: A Descriptive Essay.e: Sensory language uses words that make you see, hear, smell, taste or feel something.

Writing: A Descriptive Essay.q: Similes and metaphors are examples of ______.
Writing: A Descriptive Essay.e: Figurative language uses creative comparisons like similes and metaphors.

Writing: A Descriptive Essay.q: How many body paragraphs does a descriptive essay usually have?
Writing: A Descriptive Essay.e: The tip box says body paragraphs are usually 2-4.

Writing: A Descriptive Essay.q: Which is a good hook for a descriptive essay?
o: I don't know what to say.
The room was silent, but the air buzzed with tension.
Writing: A Descriptive Essay.e: A hook should grab attention with a striking image, like a vivid sensory sentence.

Writing: A Descriptive Essay.q: In the model essay, in which sport did Ahmed Elgendy win gold?
Writing: A Descriptive Essay.e: The model essay describes Elgendy after the tough modern pentathlon.

Writing: A Descriptive Essay.q: The conclusion of a descriptive essay should ______.
o: leave the reader with a lasting image or thought
Writing: A Descriptive Essay.e: The conclusion summarizes the impression and leaves the reader with a lasting image or thought.

Review 2.q: Scientists use satellites and radar to ______ storms.
Review 2.e: To track is to follow or watch the movement of something.

Review 2.q: Mount Everest is ______ mountain in the world.
Review 2.e: We use the superlative 'the highest' to compare one thing with all others.
The tag for 'I am' in a positive statement is 'aren't I?'.
'Never' makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive: is he?

Review 2.q: My phone, ______ has a cracked screen, still works well.
Review 2.e: Non-defining clauses with commas use 'which' for things, not 'that'.

Review 2.q: The test was ______ than I expected.
Review 2.e: 'Than' shows a comparison of two things, so we use the comparative form 'harder'.

o: having too much information to process
Review 2.e: Information overload means having too much information to process.

Review 2.q: A ______ is a system that shows you similar content based on your past activity.
Review 2.e: Algorithms show users content similar to what they engaged with before.

Ch. 1: The Mysterious Gentleman of Savil.q: In what year does the story of Phileas Fogg begin?
Ch. 1: The Mysterious Gentleman of Savil.e: The story begins in the year 1872 in London.

Ch. 1: The Mysterious Gentleman of Savil.q: What did Phileas Fogg value above all things?
Ch. 1: The Mysterious Gentleman of Savil.e: The chapter says Fogg valued calm, order and discipline above all things.

Ch. 1: The Mysterious Gentleman of Savil.q: Why did Fogg's old servant leave him?
o: He could not endure his master's strict schedule.
Ch. 1: The Mysterious Gentleman of Savil.e: His servant left suddenly, unable to endure his master's strict schedule and demands.

Ch. 1: The Mysterious Gentleman of Savil.q: Which of these jobs had Passepartout NOT tried before?
Ch. 1: The Mysterious Gentleman of Savil.e: He had been a singer, acrobat, firefighter and circus performer.

o: He was looking for his family.
Ch. 1: The Mysterious Gentleman of Savil.e: Passepartout said he left Paris because he desired peace and regularity.

Ch. 1: The Mysterious Gentleman of Savil.q: What was the only thing that seemed alive in Fogg's house?
o: the large clocks ticking in every room
Ch. 1: The Mysterious Gentleman of Savil.e: The only thing that seemed alive was the large clock in every room, all ticking in harmony.

Ch. 1: The Mysterious Gentleman of Savil.q: "A man of habit" is someone who ______.
o: follows the same routine every day
Ch. 1: The Mysterious Gentleman of Savil.e: The book explains 'a man of habit' as someone who follows the same routine every day.

Ch. 2: The Challenge at the Reform Club.q: How much money had been stolen from the Bank of England?
Ch. 2: The Challenge at the Reform Club.e: The Bank of England had been robbed of fifty-five thousand pounds.

Ch. 2: The Challenge at the Reform Club.q: Who first said one might travel around the world in eighty days or even less?
Ch. 2: The Challenge at the Reform Club.e: Andrew Stuart said that with steamships and railways one might do it in eighty days or less.

Ch. 2: The Challenge at the Reform Club.q: According to Fogg's timetable, how long would the trip from London to Suez take?
Ch. 2: The Challenge at the Reform Club.e: Fogg's timetable lists London to Suez as 7 days.

Ch. 2: The Challenge at the Reform Club.q: What was Stuart's main argument against Fogg's plan?
o: Fogg forgot storms, delays and accidents.
There were no ships to India.
Ch. 2: The Challenge at the Reform Club.e: Stuart protested that Fogg forgot storms, delays and accidents.

Ch. 2: The Challenge at the Reform Club.q: How much money did Fogg bet on the challenge?
Ch. 2: The Challenge at the Reform Club.e: Fogg said he would pay twenty thousand pounds if he failed, and receive the same if he succeeded.

Ch. 2: The Challenge at the Reform Club.q: When did Fogg promise to return to the Reform Club?
Ch. 2: The Challenge at the Reform Club.e: He said he would return on Saturday, December 21st, at the same hour.

Ch. 2: The Challenge at the Reform Club.q: The men at the club thought Fogg's challenge showed either great confidence or great ______.
Ch. 2: The Challenge at the Reform Club.e: Risking so much showed either great confidence or great madness.

Ch. 3: Across the Mediterranean to Suez.q: How did Passepartout feel when Fogg told him they were leaving?
Ch. 3: Across the Mediterranean to Suez.e: Passepartout dropped the shoes he was polishing; he had dreamed of quiet and was shocked.

Ch. 3: Across the Mediterranean to Suez.q: From which station did Fogg and Passepartout leave London?
Ch. 3: Across the Mediterranean to Suez.e: At Charing Cross Station, the train was waiting for them.

Ch. 3: Across the Mediterranean to Suez.q: Why did Detective Fix suspect Fogg?
o: Passepartout told Fix about the robbery.
Fogg looked like the description of the bank robber.
Ch. 3: Across the Mediterranean to Suez.e: The suspect's description, a tall, well-dressed Englishman with calm manners, seemed to match Fogg.

Ch. 3: Across the Mediterranean to Suez.q: Where did Fogg and Passepartout board the steamship Mongolia?
Ch. 3: Across the Mediterranean to Suez.e: At Marseilles, they boarded the steamship Mongolia, bound for Egypt.

Ch. 3: Across the Mediterranean to Suez.q: What did Fix send from Brindisi in Italy?
o: a telegram asking for an arrest warrant
Ch. 3: Across the Mediterranean to Suez.e: Fix sent a telegram asking for an arrest warrant to await Fogg in Suez.

Ch. 3: Across the Mediterranean to Suez.q: How did Fogg spend his time on board the Mongolia?
o: as if he were still in Savile Row, playing whist and reading
Ch. 3: Across the Mediterranean to Suez.e: Fogg lived exactly as if he were still in Savile Row, playing whist and reading his guidebook.
The book explains 'keep a close watch' as to observe carefully.

Ch. 4: The Desert Crossing and Cairo.q: For Mr. Fogg, Egypt was only ______.
Ch. 4: The Desert Crossing and Cairo.e: For Fogg, Egypt was only a point on a timetable, a line in his plan.

Ch. 4: The Desert Crossing and Cairo.q: What did Fix send from the telegraph office at Suez?
o: a request for an arrest warrant
Ch. 4: The Desert Crossing and Cairo.e: Fix sent an urgent message asking London to send a warrant for Fogg's arrest.

Ch. 4: The Desert Crossing and Cairo.q: What did Fix think about Fogg's challenge?
o: It was a cover to escape justice.
Ch. 4: The Desert Crossing and Cairo.e: Fix thought the challenge was just a cover and that Fogg was escaping justice.

Ch. 4: The Desert Crossing and Cairo.q: What did Fogg reply when Passepartout asked if he ever felt amazed?
o: "Amazement does not help us arrive on time."
Ch. 4: The Desert Crossing and Cairo.e: Fogg said the world is wide, but amazement does not help them arrive on time.

Ch. 4: The Desert Crossing and Cairo.q: Which sights did Passepartout enjoy in the Cairo bazaar?
o: glowing lamps, brass craftsmen and storytellers
Ch. 4: The Desert Crossing and Cairo.e: He marveled at the glowing lamps, craftsmen hammering brass and storytellers with children.
The book explains 'on schedule' as happening at the planned time.

Ch. 4: The Desert Crossing and Cairo.q: Fogg is described as "a man of precision, not of wonder". This means he ______.
o: values order and accuracy over curiosity
Ch. 4: The Desert Crossing and Cairo.e: The phrase describes someone who values order and accuracy over curiosity or amazement.

Ch. 5: The Indian Ocean and Bombay.q: Where did the Mongolia stop to take on coal at the southern tip of Arabia?
Ch. 5: The Indian Ocean and Bombay.e: The steamer reached Aden, at the southern tip of Arabia, and stopped to take on coal.

Ch. 5: The Indian Ocean and Bombay.q: How long did the voyage across the Indian Ocean last?
Ch. 5: The Indian Ocean and Bombay.e: The voyage across the Indian Ocean lasted thirteen days.

Ch. 5: The Indian Ocean and Bombay.q: What did Fogg say about the heat in the Red Sea?
o: It was of no consequence if the timetable was maintained.
Ch. 5: The Indian Ocean and Bombay.e: Fogg said the temperature was of no consequence, provided the timetable was maintained.

Ch. 5: The Indian Ocean and Bombay.q: What did Fix keep hoping to find at each port?
o: a message confirming the arrest warrant
Ch. 5: The Indian Ocean and Bombay.e: Fix hoped for a message confirming the arrest warrant, but none came.

Ch. 5: The Indian Ocean and Bombay.q: Why was Passepartout driven out of a Hindu temple in Bombay?
o: He wore his shoes on the holy ground.
Ch. 5: The Indian Ocean and Bombay.e: The priests drove him out because his shoes had polluted the holy ground.

Ch. 5: The Indian Ocean and Bombay.q: What lesson did Passepartout learn in Bombay?
Ch. 5: The Indian Ocean and Bombay.e: He realized traveling meant not only seeing wonders but also respecting unfamiliar traditions.

o: unable to choose between two feelings or actions
Ch. 5: The Indian Ocean and Bombay.e: The book explains 'torn between' as unable to choose between two feelings or actions.

Ch. 6: Across India by Rail.q: Why did the train stop in the middle of the jungle?
o: The railway line had not been completed.
Ch. 6: Across India by Rail.e: The construction had not been completed; there was no railway for fifty miles.

Ch. 6: Across India by Rail.q: How many miles of track were missing?
Ch. 6: Across India by Rail.e: The conductor said there was no railway for fifty miles.

Ch. 6: Across India by Rail.q: What was the name of the elephant Fogg hired?
Ch. 6: Across India by Rail.e: The elephant was named Kiouni, large and strong with broad ears and calm eyes.

Ch. 6: Across India by Rail.q: How much did Fogg pay to hire the elephant?
Ch. 6: Across India by Rail.e: The guide said the price was two thousand pounds, and Fogg paid without blinking.

Ch. 6: Across India by Rail.q: "Time is more valuable than gold" suggests that ______.
o: time is more important than money
Ch. 6: Across India by Rail.e: The book says this expression suggests the importance of time over money.

o: the daughter of a wealthy merchant whom Fogg rescued
Ch. 6: Across India by Rail.e: Aouda was the daughter of a wealthy merchant, and Fogg decided to rescue her.

Ch. 6: Across India by Rail.q: What did Fogg gain that was far more valuable than money and time?
Ch. 6: Across India by Rail.e: Fogg had lost money and time, but he had gained a human life saved.
